title: Triceratops horridus
summary: Triceratops horridus is a Late Cretaceous herbivorous dinosaur known for its three horns and broad skull frill.
description: This exhibit is based on the Smithsonian 3D model of Triceratops horridus Marsh, 1889. The specimen is presented as a mounted complete skeleton and is associated with material collected by John B. Hatcher in 1890 from Niobrara County, Wyoming. Triceratops belongs to Ceratopsidae and lived during the Late Cretaceous, near the end of the age of dinosaurs. Its three horns, heavy skull, and broad frill make it a strong exhibit for explaining dinosaur anatomy, defense, display, herbivorous life, and fossil discovery.
sourceInstitution: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History
